correctness.rationale: The graph is the exact 5-vertex, eight-edge wheel and the probability law includes every acyclic subset with independent positive fugacities. Independently enumerated its 134 spanning forests and computed 28 exact integer-polynomial Rayleigh differences. Five representative orbits have strictly positive polynomial coefficients; the exceptional spoke–rim orbit has the exact decomposition R=uvh(x−tS/h)^2+uvh x+tP+t²UV/h, with P,U,V positive. Positive fields make R>0. For series subdivision, Z_new=(1+a+b)Z_old(ab/(1+a+b)); conditional edge covariance is strict because a nonbridge has Z1<Z0, so induction covers all finite subdivisions. This is not derived from numerical tests.
residual_risks: Finite certificate handles only the W5 core; the infinite subdivisions rely on the analytic induction. Strictness requires each a_e>0; not full negative association.

originality.rationale: Qualified narrow PASS only for the strictly negative (equality-excluding) Rayleigh inequalities with explicit exact exceptional positive square and their strict extension to arbitrary subdivisions. Crucially, Erickson 2008 already proves arbitrary-weight NONSTRICT W5 Rayleigh via a theorem for all ≤7-vertex graphs; heterogeneous weak covariance is NOT new. The 2008 thesis SOS result is stronger in graph scope but does not on its inspected face assert strict positive-orthant separation, which the present exact certificate supplies. A possible implicit strictness corollary remains a major disclosed risk; neither the generic 2008 weak theorem nor the unit-weight Bado result explicitly states the entire strict claim.
residual_risks: Erickson 2008 Theorem 5.3.1/Corollary 5.3.2 already proves NONSTRICT I-Rayleigh for every graph on at most seven vertices, including W5 at arbitrary positive heterogeneous weights. This considerably narrows what could be new: only the full strict equality-exclusion and explicit certificate/strict subdivisions, not heterogeneous nonpositive covariance.

Erickson SOS could possibly yield strictness by an unstated positive-weight nonvanishing argument; full 114-page thesis was inspected in the relevant §§3,5 and theorem page, but all individual SOS forms were not reconstructed. This is a strong residual originality risk, not evidence that the source itself states strictness.

value.rationale: A nontrivial exact no-equality refinement on an interacting, non-series-parallel wheel is motivated because nonpositive versus strictly negative Gibbs correlations determine whether any interior equality phase exists. The exceptional spoke–rim pair has negative monomial coefficients and requires a genuine positive square certificate. Its strict subdivision propagation covers infinitely many graphs. The older 2008 ≤7-vertex SOS result substantially reduces novelty/value: neither a new general all-weight Rayleigh theorem nor novelty of series suppression is claimed.
residual_risks: The 2008 SOS could implicitly prove strictness; if so the surviving result is a recomputed special certificate and should be rejected on priority recheck.
No extension to large wheel cores, zero weights, higher-order negative association.

limitations: Strict all-positive no-equality property is a narrow enhancement to the 2008 nonstrict all-weight result; an unstated old corollary remains priority risk.
All W5 calculations are finite exact, extensions are analytic.
